title: OpenAI Jalapeño Inference Chip Challenges Nvidia’s General-Purpose AI Hardware
source_used: remio (analysis post citing OpenAI's Hot Chips presentation and interviews with Richard Ho incl. Tom's Hardware)
key_facts: OpenAI built its first custom AI accelerator, Jalapeño, with Broadcom; it is designed for inference, running trained models.
OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled it in June 2026; Richard Ho, OpenAI's vice president of hardware, gave more detail at Hot Chips 2026.
OpenAI says it went from register-transfer-level design to tape-out in nine months, against an older baseline of 18 months to two years (Ho to Tom's Hardware).
Rack of 128 accelerators, pod of 2,048; 700-watt rating, sustained draw reportedly at or below 550 watts.
OpenAI says it delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more work at peak throughput than rival platforms in selected tests with GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K2.5.
Figures come from OpenAI's testing; deployment is limited and the chip does not replace Nvidia hardware used for training.
quote_evidence: OpenAI designed its first custom accelerator in nine months, creating a direct challenge to the general-purpose hardware that powers most large AI services.
OpenAI still has much to prove.
OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled Jalapeño in June 2026 as the first processor in a planned, multigeneration computing platform.
why_it_matters_hint: Custom inference chips let AI labs cut cost and power per answer, but OpenAI's numbers are self-reported.
event_date: Jun 2026 (unveiling); Hot Chips 2026 presentation (date not stated)
notes: Analysis post re-covering a June 2026 announcement and a Hot Chips talk; not new this week. Read the first ~10,000 of 23,800 characters. Original sources (OpenAI, Tom's Hardware) not opened.
